**Verdict: none of the three solutions is correct.** Solutions 1 and 2 give the same value, k₀(1/c − 1), and Solution 3 gives a value twice the one I obtain.

**Local shift.** Freeze coefficients at a point with local orthonormal frame (e₁ = e_η, e₂ = e_φ, n). The only order −1 contribution to the projection onto the +k₀ eigenvector e₊ = (e₁ + in)/√2 comes from the scalar term a(z·n)I/|z|³, with a = μ/(4πM). Its 2D Fourier symbol is aπκ₂/|ξ|, where κ₂ = (cos η − ξ)/c. The zz^T term projects to zero at this order, and the skew term has no order −1 part. Checking the normalization: for the unit sphere this gives eigenvalues ≈ 1/(4n) for the classical NP kernel, matching the known 1/(2(2n+1)).

With physical frequency |ξ| = |ℓ|ψ/ξ, the eigenvalue for each branch is

ν_ℓ(η) ≈ k₀ + s(η)/|ℓ|, s(η) = (k₀ξ/(2c))·n_ρ(η), n_ρ = (cos η − ξ)/(1 − ξ cos η).

This is the same for ℓ > 0 and ℓ < 0. So s is not the constant k₀ξ/(2c)·(mean of n_ρ), and it changes sign: eigenvalues lie below k₀ only where n_ρ < 0.

**Counting.** Weyl's law gives

N(t) ~ (1/(2π)) ∫₀^{2π} 2·[−s(η)]₊/t dη, so lim t·N(t) = (1/π)∫₀^{2π}[−s]₊ dη.

Averaging s, as Solutions 1 and 2 do, is wrong because only the positive part of −s contributes.

**Integral.** Using (ξ − cos η)/(1 − ξ cos η) = (1/ξ)[1 − c²/(1 − ξ cos η)] and ∫_{cos η<ξ} dη/(1 − ξ cos η) = π/c, the integral over {cos η < ξ} is (1/ξ)(2π − 2 arccos ξ − πc). Therefore

lim_{t↓0} t·N_k(t) = (μ/(4(2μ+λ)))·[(π + 2 arcsin ξ)/(π√(1−ξ²)) − 1],

independent of k.

**Assessment of the solutions.**
- Solutions 1 and 2 use the signed mean of the subprincipal term, which ignores the sign change of the local shift. Their value k₀(1/c − 1) is therefore not the limit.
- Solution 3 has the right structure (positive part of the local shift, same integral), but its local coefficient is twice the value I obtain: its projection e₊*Be₊ = −k₀ξn_ρ/(πc) should be −k₀ξn_ρ/(2πc), which gives the factor of 2.

I did not verify this numerically, so the result rests on the local symbol computation and the sphere normalization check.
